about.title: Calabasas Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Calabasas residents rely on a mix of local urgent care clinics and larger Los Angeles County hospital systems for everything from routine checkups to emergency surgery. Most visits go fine, but when a physician, surgeon, or hospital staff member deviates from the accepted standard of care, the results can be lasting — a missed diagnosis, a surgical complication, or a medication error that never should have happened. Sorting out whether a bad outcome was simply an unavoidable risk or the result of actual negligence takes a qualified medical expert and a careful review of records, which is exactly the kind of work an experienced malpractice attorney is built to do. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a cut of any settlement — we simply connect Calabasas residents who believe they were harmed by a medical provider with an independent attorney who can evaluate the claim and explain, in plain terms, what comes next under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Documentation Matter in Calabasas Cases

items.title: MICRA's Short Discovery Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to file — an attorney can help you figure out where you stand before that window closes.

items.title: The 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed in California, the provider typically must receive 90 days' advance written notice, which means early legal guidance isn't optional — it's part of the process.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises Yearly
items.desc: California law caps non-economic damages in malpractice cases, though that cap increases annually, so understanding the current figure and how it applies to your situation matters when weighing a claim.

items.question: How do I know if my bad medical outcome was actually malpractice?
items.answer: Not every disappointing result from surgery or treatment counts as malpractice — California law requires proof that a provider deviated from the accepted standard of care and that this deviation caused harm. This almost always requires a qualified medical expert to review the records and offer an opinion. An independent attorney can help arrange that review before you decide whether to move forward.

items.question: Are there Calabasas-specific hospitals or providers this applies to?
items.answer: Calabasas residents typically receive care at nearby Los Angeles County medical facilities and specialist clinics rather than large hospitals within the city itself, since Calabasas is a smaller community. The claim process and California legal deadlines apply the same way regardless of which specific provider or facility was involved.

items.question: What if I already missed the 90-day notice period?
items.answer: The 90-day pre-suit notice rule is one of several procedural steps in California malpractice claims, but missing a step doesn't automatically end your options — it depends on your specific timeline and discovery date. An attorney can review the dates involved and tell you honestly whether you still have a path forward.
